# The negation of an interval, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_neg_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An interval $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ that contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, with $X = [x_l, x_u]$. An interval may be unbounded, and empty.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, -x : x \in X \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $z_l = z_{l0} + z_{l1}$, $z_u = z_{u0} + z_{u1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-X` | `Interval<T, 2>` | `Interval<T, 2>` | `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **I1.** The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- **I2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ is.
- **I3.** $Z$ contains $-x$ for every $x \in X$, unbounded operands included (their members are real numbers).
- **I4.** For nonempty $X$, where $\ell$ and $h$ are the greatest lower bound and the least upper bound of the exact range $\{\, -x : x \in X \,\}$, as extended real numbers: $z_l = \ell$ and $z_u = h$, exactly.
- **I5.** For bounded $X$, $Z$ is bounded exactly when every member $z$ of the exact range satisfies $\lvert z\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max}}$. The conditions are on the exact values of the operands, and $2^{e_{\max}}$ is the overflow threshold of `T`, just above its largest finite number: $2^{e_{\max}}$ is $2^{1024}$ for `double`, $2^{128}$ for `float`.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_neg_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalExact.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalExact.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_neg_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_neg_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** neg_2 of each bound, exchanged (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_neg_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_neg_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`neg_2`](neg_2.md).

```
# The negation of an interval with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "Interval kernels", "Two limbs"):
# neg_2 of each bound, exchanged. Exact; the empty set ((+inf, 0), (-inf, 0)) is its own negation,
# with the signs of its zeros changed. A bounded operand gives a bounded result: a finite canonical
# 2-limb value is below the overflow threshold 2^(qmax + p) in magnitude (its leading limb is at
# most Omega and its second within half a gap of it, a tie going away from Omega), so every member
# of -X is, and the condition of bounded_when, with exp 0, holds exactly when the result is bounded.
# For every precision.

(zl0, zl1) = neg_2(xu0, xu1)
(zu0, zu1) = neg_2(xl0, xl1)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#interval_neg_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 1 115 351 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
